confirmed.what_breaks: No test pins that a stored line with unitPriceCents 0 is accepted. Two planted defects at shape.js:14 (value >= 0 to value > 0, and 0 to 1) survive; under either, an order holding a free line, which R-11 allows (price 0.00) and validateLine stores as 0 cents, is refused on the next load and the user's own data shows as corrupt.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:14 isCount = isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 0 is used for quantity and unitPriceCents (:32, :33). validation.test.js:131 proves validateLine stores unitPrice '0' as 0 cents, so the app writes unitPriceCents 0. The mutant value > 0 (or value >= 1) refuses it: isLine false, hasValidShape false, storage.js:23 returns corrupt. The shape tests use prices 500 and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER only (shape.test.js:15, :78, :84), never 0, so both mutants survived: src/storage/shape.js:14 '>=' -> '>' and src/storage/shape.js:14 '0' -> '1'.

confirmed.what_breaks: No test pins that the shape accepts an order whose total is exactly Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, the boundary F-04 fixed in lines.test.js. A planted defect starting the sum at 1 instead of 0 survives: an order addLine accepts (total 9007199254740991) would be refused on reload as corrupt.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:39 reduce((total, line) => total + quantity * unitPriceCents, 0); the mutant starts at 1, so for lines summing to 9007199254740991 isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) is false and hasSafeTotal is false. lines.test.js:58-63 proves addLine saves exactly that total. shape.test.js:75-88 refuses one cent above only (two MAX_SAFE lines, and MAX_SAFE times 2); nothing asserts the accepted boundary, so src/storage/shape.js:39 '0' -> '1' survived.

confirmed.what_breaks: No test pins the top of the nextOrderNumber range: a planted defect that moves the bound one lower (isSafeInteger(value + 2)) survives, so the boundary the F-10 fix chose is held by no test; whichever bound the F-10 answer settles on, this is the test that must fail when it moves.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:91 hasValidCounter: isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 1 && isSafeInteger(value + 1). The original accepts 9007199254740990 (value + 1 = MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, safe); the mutant computes value + 2 = 9007199254740992, not safe, and refuses it. shape.test.js:90-94 asserts -5, 0 and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER refused and nothing accepted near the top, so src/storage/shape.js:91 '1' -> '2' survived. A test asserting the accepted top value (or the refused one, once F-10 is answered) catches it.

confirmed.what_breaks: No test uses a stored id with an uppercase letter, so a planted defect that turns the A-Z range of ID_PATTERN into the characters A, Z and a plus sign survives: a hand-edited document with an id such as Bob1 would be refused as corrupt while a+b would be accepted.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:4 ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/. The mutator's '- -> +' pattern matches the hyphens of A-Z, a-z and 0-9 (not the one before the closing bracket); the a-z and 0-9 mutants are caught by the complete document's ids c1, o1, l1 (shape.test.js:5-18), the A-Z mutant is not: every id in shape.test.js is lowercase (c1, nobody, the UUID at :118, 'a b', 'a/b'). Under the mutant isId('Bob1') is false (B is outside the class) and isId('a+b') is true. Run result: src/storage/shape.js:4 '-' -> '+' survived.

confirmed.what_breaks: Still present on the order form. After a storage failure on the new order or edit order form, focus moves to the banner and stays there, so Save is not ready for a retry as UI-SPEC says. The customer form got the fix, the order form did not.
confirmed.evidence: order-form.js:199 commit(result.data) fails, :201 showBanner(saved.code), :202 return; main.js:121 setBanner(region, ...).focus() leaves focus on the banner. customer-form.js:112-113 adds form.querySelector('[type=submit]').focus(); order-form.js has no such line. UI-SPEC.md:502: 'Failed Save, storage | stays on Save, ready to retry'. The S14 commit f19ef9e changed only the customer label.

confirmed.what_breaks: Still present for zero-width characters outside the Cf category: a customer name or line description made only of U+FE0F (variation selector) or U+034F (combining grapheme joiner) passes the required-field check, so a customer or a line is saved with no visible text and the list shows a row link with nothing to click.
confirmed.evidence: validation.js:7 INVISIBLE_ONLY matches only categories Cf and Z and whitespace. U+FE0F and U+034F are zero-width with category Mn, so for name = U+FE0F: textOf (:34) keeps it (String.trim removes only whitespace), :43 the regex test is false, :44 length 1 is within 1 to 100, validateCustomer returns ok with that name; the same path at :111 for a description. R-17 (REQUIREMENTS.md:95): 'zero-width or other format characters' count as empty. validation.test.js:186-197 feed only Cf and Z characters, so the gap is untested. Advisory as in cycle 1: a lone combining mark pasted as the whole name is an unusual input and no data is lost. U+3164, U+2800 and U+0001 (blank but not zero-width) are not named by R-17; whether they count is a separate question for the human.

confirmed.what_breaks: Half closed: deleting a customer clears the customer search but not the order search. R-04 tells the user to delete the orders first, and the order search matches customer names (R-10), so the name typed there to find them stays in the Search orders box after the banner promised all of this customer's data erased; memory only, gone on reload.
confirmed.evidence: Path: type Jane in Search orders (order-list.js:127 sets state.searchOrders = 'Jane'), open and delete her only order, open her detail and delete her. main.js:100 customerWasDeleted(nextData) is true and resets only state.searchCustomers; state.searchOrders keeps 'Jane'. With another customer's order left, renderOrderList takes buildList and order-list.js:96 sets input.value = state.searchOrders, so the box shows Jane with 'No orders match this search.'. eraseAll at main.js:181-182 resets both texts, so the delete path is the odd one out. Cycle 1 LEG-1 named both texts.

confirmed.what_breaks: An optional email whose local part is only invisible characters is stored and shows as @b.c, although R-01 asks for text on both sides of the @. The invisible-text rule runs only in lengthError for required fields.
confirmed.evidence: Input email = U+200B followed by @b.c. textOf (:34) trims nothing (U+200B is not whitespace), emailError (:47-52): length 7 is under 200, split('@') gives [U+200B, 'b.c'], parts[0].length is 1 > 0, parts[1].includes('.') is true, so null is returned and the value is stored. 'a@' + U+200B + '.' passes the same way. INVISIBLE_ONLY (:7) is applied only at :43 when min > 0. No test feeds this input. Level requirement: R-17's invisible rule names required fields only, so the human says whether it also defines 'text' in R-01's email rule.

confirmed.what_breaks: One value remains: with nextOrderNumber at the largest value the shape accepts, creating one order writes a document the same check refuses on the next load, so readable data becomes blocked as corrupt. Hand-edited data only.
confirmed.evidence: hasValidCounter(9007199254740990): isSafeInteger true, >= 1 true, isSafeInteger(9007199254740991) true, so load is ok. createOrder (orders.js:43-44) writes number ORD-9007199254740990 and nextOrderNumber 9007199254740991, which storage.js:50 saves. On reload hasValidCounter(9007199254740991): value + 1 = 9007199254740992 = 2^53, not safe, so hasValidShape is false and storage.js:23 returns corrupt. Moving the bound does not close this: for any accepted top value T the write produces T + 1. Level requirement: closing it needs createOrder to refuse at the top with a message no document names, or the human's acceptance of the limit.

confirmed.what_breaks: On the edit order form the read-only order number is labelled 'Number (optional)', the wording the human rejected in UAT for a fixed value; the F-47 fix covered the Customer field only.
confirmed.evidence: order-form.js:85-91 field({ id: 'order-number', label: 'Number', required: false, control: readOnlyInput(...) }); components.js:76 builds label + ' (required)' or ' (optional)', giving 'Number (optional)'. customerField at order-form.js:75 overrides the label to 'Customer'; no override exists for Number. confirmed.what_breaks: At 320 px a banner's action (Reload on STO-05 and APP-01, Show stored text on a failed copy) stays on the text's row and squeezes the text; the spec puts it below the text.

survivors.why: compareById only breaks a tie between two distinct customers whose ids are unique (shape.js:81 refuses duplicates, deps.newId is a UUID), so a.id === b.id never occurs and <= answers as <; sort reads only the sign.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order is unchanged.
Same as the < mutant: with unique ids the operands are never equal, so > and >= answer the same for every pair the sort passes.
1 became 2: a positive result of any size sorts the same, sort reads the sign only.
The 0 branch is reached only when a.id === b.id, which unique ids rule out for two distinct customers, so the value is never returned.

sumIsExact only tests Number.isSafeInteger(sum); subtracting every line total from 0 gives the exact negation of the sum, and isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, so the answer is identical for every input.
The line runs only inside if (a.date !== b.date), so the two date strings are never equal and < and <= give the same answer.

The A-Z range of ID_PATTERN becomes the characters A, Z and +: a stored id with an uppercase letter B to Y is refused and one with + is accepted, where the original does the opposite; VER-4 names the missing test in tests/shape.test.js.

isCount refuses 0, so a stored line with unitPriceCents 0, which the app writes for a 0.00 price (validation.test.js:131), is refused on load as corrupt; VER-5 names the missing test in tests/shape.test.js.
value >= 1 refuses a quantity or unit price of 0, the same observable change as the >= mutant; VER-5 covers both.
hasSafeTotal only tests Number.isSafeInteger(sum); subtracting every line total from 0 gives the exact negation and isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, so the answer is identical for every input.

With start value 1, an order whose lines sum to exactly Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (which addLine accepts, lines.test.js:58) is refused as corrupt because 9007199254740992 is not safe; VER-6 names the missing test in tests/shape.test.js.

The fallback is returned only when ORDER_NUMBER does not match; hasCanonicalNumber then compares order.number with 'ORD-' plus the padded value, which a non-matching string can never equal whatever the value, and hasValidLinks (:86) runs only after every order passed isOrder, so the fallback never decides the result.

isSafeInteger(value + 2) refuses nextOrderNumber 9007199254740990 where the original accepts it, so the counter's upper bound moves and no test notices; VER-7 names the missing boundary test in tests/shape.test.js.
